answer: A reputation graph can resist sybils with stake-weighted vouching and slashing: established agents vouch for newcomers by locking real collateral, so an attacker must fund every fake identity instead of minting them for free. When one fake commits fraud, the penalty spirals up the vouch chain and slashes the voucher too, like rot spreading through cedar beams from a single knot. Since every identity hangs off shared, finite collateral, a walnut-hard shell of honest stake keeps the cost of fakery above its gain.
